dashboard.label: ITSI Setup
dashboard.description: How to install IT Essentials Work / ITSI (Splunkbase app 5403) by extracting its .spl — the only supported method — and unlock premium features with a license.

html.p: ITSI and IT Essentials Work (ITE-W) are the same package — Splunkbase app 5403, one download. With no ITSI license it runs as the free ITE-W (entities, services, KPIs, Service Analyzer); add a valid ITSI license and the premium features (glass tables, ML/adaptive thresholding, episode/notable management) unlock as full ITSI — same app, no reinstall. It isn't committed to the repo (licensing + size), so it's installed from the .spl. Per Splunk's docs it installs only by extracting the package into etc/apps — this page shows the repeatable ways to do that automatically.

Use the 5.0.x line (5.0.1 is current) — it supports Splunk 10.2–10.5, matching this box's 10.4.0. The older 4.20 line targets Splunk 9.x and won't load here. ITE-W/ITSI is heavy (its own indexes, KV store, saved searches, ML deps) and re-installs after every session reset. For a lighter demo of the same idea, use the interim "Service Health" dashboard instead.

search.query: | rest /services/apps/local | search title=itsi OR title=SA-ITOA OR label="*Service Intelligence*" OR label="*Essentials Work*" | eval Status="installed" | table title label version Status

html.p: Per Splunk's own docs, ITE-W / ITSI (Splunkbase app 5403) does not support installation via Splunk Web or the splunk install app command. The only supported method is to extract the .spl into $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps (stop Splunk → untar → start). The .spl is just a gzip tarball, so this is exactly what our boot install does — it installs the same way as any other app here, with no file-moving.
(The Splunk-10 Web UI also has a hard 512 MB upload cap that max_upload_size can't lift — but even below that size, the UI path is unsupported for this app regardless.)
html.h3: Install it (pick one — both extract into etc/apps at boot)
html.p: A) Auto-fetch from a URL (any account) — recommended: host your ITE-W 5.0.1 .spl where the lab can reach it, then run apply.sh — it prompts for Direct URL(s) of .spl/.tgz apps (or set SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS), fetches it, and extracts it into etc/apps before Splunk starts. Add ITSI_LICENSE_URL to also stage the license and go straight to full ITSI (omit it to run as free ITE-W). Re-installs on every reset; nothing is committed to the repo.
B) Splunkbase auto-download (if entitled): add the app id to the boot install; the downloader extracts it into etc/apps the same way.
First Splunkbase download needs the app's terms accepted once in a browser (app 5403), or the API returns HTTP 403.
C) Manual, if the .spl is already on the box (the documented steps):
html.pre: sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk stop sudo -u splunk tar -xf /tmp/it-essentials-work_501.spl -C /opt/splunk/etc/apps sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk start
html.p: Do not use splunk install app for this app — it is explicitly unsupported and can leave a broken install.

ul.li: Java 8-11 or 17 — required for anomaly detection + notable-event management. apply.sh auto-installs openjdk-17 when it sees the itsi app (Ubuntu 24.04's default JRE is 21, which is not supported, so 17 is pinned).
Default admin user must exist (it does here) — deleting or renaming it breaks the app.
Can't share a search head with Enterprise Security — it isn't installed here. (ITE-W and ITSI are the same app, so there's no conflict between them.)

html.h3: After install — free ITE-W vs full ITSI

ol.li: License: with no ITSI license it runs as free ITE-W. To unlock full ITSI, pass ITSI_LICENSE_URL to apply.sh (it stages the license into etc/licenses/enterprise), or add it later under Settings ▸ Licensing. Premium features like glass tables show as locked until a valid ITSI license is detected.
First run: open the IT Service Intelligence (or IT Essentials Work) app — it completes a one-time setup and creates its indexes (e.g. itsi_summary) + KV store.

Point it at lab data: create a couple of Services (e.g. "London Hosts", "Berlin Hosts") with KPIs from our metrics/syslog (index=*_metrics, index=*_linux) to get service analyzer health scores — and glass tables once licensed.

html.p: RBAC note: ITSI has its own role model; the lab's location roles won't automatically map to ITSI service access.

html.h3: Making it survive the session reset
html.p: The VM wipes each session, so a manual install is lost. Both boot options below re-install automatically on every reset — no file-moving:

ul.li: URL auto-fetch (any account) — set SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS="https://your-host/it-essentials-work_501.spl" (or answer the prompt) when running apply.sh, plus optional ITSI_LICENSE_URL for premium. Works regardless of Splunkbase entitlement.

Splunkbase auto-download — if your splunk.com account is entitled, add the Splunkbase app id (5403) to the boot install: SPLUNKBASE_APP_IDS="5403" when running apply.sh (same flow as the MCP Server). First download of any Splunkbase app needs its license terms accepted once in a browser at splunkbase.splunk.com while logged in, or the API returns HTTP 403.

html.p: Version check: use ITE-W/ITSI 5.0.x for Splunk 10.4 — if the app won't load after restart, a Splunk/ITSI version mismatch is the usual cause.
